operator_io_quirks: Table names are lowercase but quoted in DDL ("list", "teachers"); 'list' is a Python builtin and a SQL-ish word — keep original spelling, always double-quote.
Column names are mixed-case (LastName, FirstName, Grade, Classroom); lookup must be case-insensitive (.lower()) but emit original spelling.
Both tables have composite PKs (LastName, FirstName) — PK-duplicate dropping must compare tuples, not single columns.
No FKs at all; process_order yields two independent level-0 tables; table_order/column_order must still be deterministic (sorted).
All columns notnull=0 despite being PK members — sqlite PK on TEXT allows NULLs in non-INTEGER PK; TS may insert NULL PK parts and they will succeed.
FirstName values carry a LEADING SPACE (' PATRINA', ' JEROME') — string fuzzer's contaminate/prefix ops and literal pool must preserve it; trimming would change denotation.
Grade is INTEGER with values 0..6 (distinct 7); Classroom INTEGER 101..112 — Number fuzzer will draw from full [-10^scale,10^scale] range, wildly outside these.
No unique/check constraints, no indexes, no views/triggers — write_instance_sqlite has nothing to fail on except PK duplicates (which are pre-dropped).
Tiny tables (60 and 12 rows) — choose_table_sizes will produce 1..~2500 rows, far larger than originals; original_values sampling (k=5) will heavily repeat.
Storage class matches declared type everywhere (text/integer) — no affinity contradictions to survive.
No dangling FKs, no self-references, no missing parents — the FK-consistency path is exercised only trivially (no FK columns).
DDL uses tab/newline formatting inside CREATE TABLE — line-based unique/check scan must not misfire on 'PRIMARY KEY(...)' lines.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer on LastName/FirstName: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length 0..20, plus 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/around/drop-char) — will produce names unlike the real ones and often with stray spaces.
Number fuzzer on Grade/Classroom: scale=0 so range [-1,1] for ints; perturb +-1/+-2 — Grade will be ~{-2..2}, Classroom ~{-2..2}, i.e. implausible classrooms (real 101..112) and grades (real 0..6).
Composite PK (LastName,FirstName) -> max_l0 = 30 per member; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate tuples, so with 60-row originals and 5-element pools, many rows collapse.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed Grade/Classroom with real values (0..6, 101..112) and names; p=0.2 means ~20% fresh, 80% element — but element set is only 5 originals + distinct pool values.
No FKs -> fill_foreign_keys_consistently never runs; instance is just per-column independent sampling.
Likely FN driver: Classroom values outside 101..112 make 'classroom = 101' style predicates return empty or wrong rows; Grade outside 0..6 similarly.
Likely FP driver: with only 7 distinct grades and 12 classrooms, TS's small element pool + PK collapse can accidentally make two different queries agree (missing ties/duplicates).
Leading-space FirstName: TS string fuzzer's 'drop first char' contaminate turns ' PATRINA' into 'PATRINA', changing equality/join semantics vs gold.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforced in Python; but PK on TEXT allows NULL, so NULL PK parts may slip through and survive insert — upstream behaviour preserved.
Table sizes up to ~2500 vs 60/12 originals: aggregate queries (COUNT, AVG) will differ in magnitude from gold on original, but TS compares query-vs-query on the SAME instance, so that's fine.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like strings — irrelevant here since names are non-numeric.
